card.name: Verb after a subject, before a clause
card.fires_on: A verb (could, would, were, involved, constituted, included, was) right after a noun or pronoun subject, where a past participle or reduced clause could follow. It appears in formal or instructional text.

modes.description: A past-tense or participle verb right after a noun, starting a reduced relative clause.

modes.label: Verb after a short subject
modes.description: A verb like was, think or included after a short subject in a quoted or explanatory sentence.
modes.example: Who did Atticus<< think>> killed Bob Ewell?

card.writes: It pushes toward words like originally and previously, which are past-time adverbs, and away from email and list-style tokens.
card.plain: It fires on the verb that follows a subject in formal sentences, just before the clause continues.
